main_text.p: Verùm quum Xerxes in Græciam vê-nit, ut ajunt ipsi Thebani ad tuendum honorem suum contra Platæenses Μηδισμὸν fibi exprobrantes, populi potestate oppressa, pauci potentes contra leges & instituta majorum rempu-blicam occupaverant, & civitatem in barbarorum partes concedere coëge-rant. Sed expulsis è Græciâ Persis, legi-bus & juri populi locus rursum datus: ifque status deinceps conservatus. Ple-rasque verò Bœotiæ civitates alias in optimatum fuisse potestate tempore belli Peloponnesiaci, unus Thucydidis locus, qui est libro quarto, nos docet. Sic enim habet, quosdam earum civita-tum rerum novarum avidos cum duo-bus ducibus Atticis Hippocrate & De-mosthene clàm consilia agitasse & con-venìsse de statu civitatum suarum præ-senti in popularem, qualis Athenis erat, commutando. Sed Thebas senatum quoq; suum publici consilii ducem ha-buisse, & per magistratus definiti tem-poris munera reipublicæ domi & foris, pace ac bello administrasse, ut solent civitates liberæ, hinc illinc cognoscere promptum est.Inter cæteras verò Bœo-tiæ civitates Thebana hæc ita caput cre-scente fortunâ extulit, ut ex sociâ pene dominâ se iis imposuerit, certe ἀξίωμα aliq

page.notes: Printed text is in plain Latin, with long s normalised to s. The first word is treated as a continuation from the previous page (cont="true"); the page opens mid-sentence. The Greek "Μηδισμὸν" and "ἀξίωμα" are copied as seen; the accents on the scan are small and may not be exact. The catchword "aliq" (for aliquam) is at the foot; it is also the start of the next page's first word, so it is kept only in the bottom margin, not in the text. Bottom-right margin marks ("ɔ19ere", "ɔ19ɔɛlɛ", "LG") are too faint and damaged to read with confidence and are not transcribed as notes. The tiny marks in the left margin are printer's or ornamental marks, not legible text. The right edge is a dark binding shadow, not text.
